title: the weaver's son
narrativeQuestion: The machines came for the best paid workers in England. What happened to them, and to their children, after they lost?

chapters.title: The best paid workers in town
chapters.claim: Croppers and handloom weavers were skilled and well paid around 1806.

chapters.title: Then the machines arrived
chapters.claim: Power looms and shearing frames let untrained workers do skilled work, and the price of hand weaving collapsed.

chapters.title: A warning signed Ned Ludd
chapters.claim: Luddite letters named targets, warned first and hid behind a made up name.

chapters.title: Hammers in the night
chapters.claim: Luddites smashed about 1,000 frames and chose their targets.

chapters.title: Machine breaking becomes a hanging crime
chapters.claim: Parliament answered with the death penalty and 12,000 soldiers.

chapters.title: Twenty two months
chapters.claim: The uprising spread across the north and ended at the gallows in Lancaster and York.

chapters.title: What a week's pay could buy
chapters.claim: One weaver's real wages fell by more than two thirds from 1797 to 1834.

chapters.title: The weaver's son
chapters.claim: Weavers had nowhere to go, raised their children to a dying trade, and the croppers were replaced by children.

chapters.title: So who came out ahead?
chapters.claim: Owners and buyers gained while workers waited a generation, and Ricardo admitted machines could hurt workers.

chapters.title: Now it's your trade
chapters.claim: Workers who understand the work well enough to direct the machine come out ahead.

chapters.title: Fix the notes
chapters.claim: Four common beliefs about the Luddites are wrong.

accuracyNotes: The boy who wove three and a half pieces is presented as a claim that spread through the weaving districts.
Wage figures from the 1830s come from testimony to Parliament and vary by town and cloth.
Abraham Charlson is listed as 16 in contemporary records, and his family claimed he was younger.
The MIT study is described as small and not yet peer reviewed when released.
